appOverview: Login is the entry screen for anyone who opens the app without an active session: a centered card with the app name, an email field, a masked password field with a show/hide toggle, a Sign in button, a non-functional 'Forgot your password?' placeholder link, and an error area that stays hidden until a login attempt fails. Successful login starts a server-side session (session_id cookie) and redirects to /dashboard. Other views rely on that session to know who is signed in (e.g. Dashboard's 'Bienvenido, <nombre>') and to end it on logout. There is no registration view yet — QA accounts are inserted directly.

elementSpecs.behavior: Static text showing the app name/logo at the top of the card. No user interaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Is visible on the login screen at all times

elementSpecs.behavior: Free-text field for the account email. Validated client-side before any request is sent.
businessRules: Required: submitting while empty shows an inline validation message next to the field and sends no request
Must look like an email (contains '@' with at least one character after it) before submit is allowed; otherwise shows an inline validation message and sends no request
dataNeeds: users.email (pending verification against the real schema — table doesn't exist yet, see schema-changes.sql)
acceptanceCriteria: Shows an inline error and does not submit if left empty
Shows an inline error and does not submit if the value has no '@' or nothing after the '@'
Clears its inline error once corrected to a non-empty, email-shaped value

elementSpecs.behavior: Masked free-text field for the account password. Content can be revealed via password-toggle-button.
businessRules: Required: submitting while empty shows an inline validation message next to the field and sends no request
dataNeeds: users.password_hash (pending verification against the real schema)
acceptanceCriteria: Shows an inline error and does not submit if left empty
Clears its inline error once corrected to a non-empty value
Renders as masked characters by default

elementSpecs.behavior: Toggles password-input between masked and plain-text rendering. Purely client-side, no request involved.
businessRules: Toggling never clears or alters the typed password value, only its visual rendering
acceptanceCriteria: Reveals password-input as plain text after one click
Masks password-input again after a second click

elementSpecs.behavior: Runs client-side validation on email-input and password-input; if both pass, sends the login request and enters a loading/disabled state until a response arrives, then reflects the outcome (redirect, or an error shown via login-error-message).
businessRules: Disabled and showing a loading state while the request is in flight, so a double-click can't send two requests
On success (valid credentials, account not locked): the server starts a session for that user (session_id cookie) and the client redirects to /dashboard
On failure due to wrong email/password combination: shows the generic message 'Incorrect email or password' via login-error-message — never reveals which of the two fields was wrong

After 5 failed attempts in a row for the same account, the next attempt (even with the correct password) shows 'This account has been locked due to too many failed attempts. Contact support.' via login-error-message
A successful login resets that account's failed-attempt counter back to zero
dataNeeds: users.failed_attempts (pending verification against the real schema)
users.is_locked (pending verification against the real schema)
acceptanceCriteria: Does not send a request if either field fails client-side validation
Shows a loading state and is disabled from click until the response arrives
Redirects to /dashboard after a response indicating valid, non-locked credentials
A successful response is accompanied by a session identifying the signed-in user (verified via session-guard, not by inspecting the cookie's contents)
Shows 'Incorrect email or password' after a wrong-credentials response, without indicating which field was wrong
Shows 'This account has been locked due to too many failed attempts. Contact support.' after the 6th consecutive failed attempt, even if that 6th attempt used the correct password
A successful login resets the account's failed-attempt counter to zero

elementSpecs.behavior: Present below login-button as a placeholder. Does nothing when clicked.
businessRules: Out of scope for this view: no navigation, no request, per description_login.md
acceptanceCriteria: Is present and visible below login-button on first load
Does not navigate and sends no request when clicked

elementSpecs.behavior: Non-visual, backend-owned concern (not a rendered component in this screen): given a request's session_id cookie, determines whether it identifies a currently signed-in user and, if so, that user's identity (at least full_name). Every authenticated view (starting with Dashboard) uses this to gate access and to render 'who is signed in'.
businessRules: A missing, invalid, or previously-invalidated session_id must resolve to 'not signed in' — never partial or stale identity
Resolves to the signed-in user's full_name (users.full_name), not just an opaque id, so views don't need a second round-trip to display a name
Session data lives in an in-process store (InMemorySessionRepository), never persisted to Postgres, per tecnologias/tecnologia_bbdd.md
acceptanceCriteria: Resolves to 'not signed in' when no session_id cookie is present
Resolves to 'not signed in' when session_id doesn't match any active session
Resolves to the signed-in user's full_name when session_id matches an active session
Resolves to 'not signed in' for a session_id that was previously ended via logout-session

elementSpecs.behavior: Non-visual, backend-owned capability (not a rendered component in this screen): ends an active session server-side. Triggered later by the Dashboard view's 'Salir' element, which lives outside this view — this view only owns the session lifecycle, not that button.
businessRules: Invalidates the session server-side (removed from the in-memory store) so session-guard immediately resolves it to 'not signed in'
A session_id that has already been logged out, or never existed, is treated the same as any other 'not signed in' case — no error distinguishing them, to avoid leaking session existence
acceptanceCriteria: After logout-session runs for a given session_id, session-guard resolves that same session_id to 'not signed in'
Running logout-session again for an already-ended (or unknown) session_id doesn't error and still results in 'not signed in'

elementSpecs.behavior: Hidden by default; becomes visible only after a failed login response, showing whichever generic message applies.
businessRules: Shows exactly one of the two defined messages — never both, never a field-specific one
acceptanceCriteria: Is not visible on first load
Becomes visible showing 'Incorrect email or password' after a wrong-credentials response
Becomes visible showing 'This account has been locked due to too many failed attempts. Contact support.' after a locked-account response

globalRules: No 'remember me' checkbox and no social login (Google/GitHub/etc.) in this view — explicitly out of scope per description_login.md
The client never indicates which of email/password was incorrect for a wrong-credentials response — same generic message either way (security requirement)
This view's responsibility ends at a successful login; /dashboard itself is a separate, not-yet-implemented view
Registration is a separate, future view — for now, QA test accounts are inserted directly into the users table
Session mechanism is session_id cookie + in-memory store (no JWT, no express-session, per tecnologia_code.md/tecnologia_bbdd.md) — this was already the intended design, only now being implemented
A signed-out or never-existed session must never be distinguishable from each other in any response — same as the email/password non-disclosure rule above, applied to session state
